title: Choose the visual world
question: Your brief pins the look (hand-drawn like the cards, minimal, near-wordless). These are different ways the UI can live inside that look. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pantomime Strip
options.lineage: wordless comic strips and pantomime cartoons
options.thesis: Each screen is one wordless comic panel: the card acts, the UI only draws the motion lines.
options.viewport: Play: the screen is one ink-bordered panel, the card at ~80% height in the middle; spin and flip are small pictogram balloons pointing at the card; back is a curled arrow in the gutter.
options.risk: Comic devices multiply fast; held to one device per action or the card loses the stage.

raised.raise: Colour lives only in the card: every UI mark is black ink on white.
One hot yellow, reserved for the spot you can use right now.
One surface: the picked card's panel grows into the play view, no page change felt.
Fixed HUD slots: back, mode and restart never move; only their glyph changes state.
The artist credit rides on each card as a small hand-lettered tag.
Spot states drawn as stages: locked is hatched, usable glows, used gets a tick.

options.label: Card Furniture
options.lineage: the cards' own icons: flip triangle, spin swirl, door arrow, title sticker
options.thesis: The UI is built only from glyphs the cards already teach, so learning one card teaches the app.
materials: white sticker boxes with thick black outline
flat field taking each card's main colour
options.viewport: Play: the card on a flat field tinted from its own art; flip triangles sit outside the card edges, spin swirls beside it, a white title-sticker back button top-left.
options.risk: Closest to the cards themselves, so the least surprising; the per-card field colour can fight dark cards.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Levels as departure rows that clack into place.
options.viewport: Picker as a board of rows; play behind a steel frame.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the board is all lettering, the opposite of a wordless kids' game, and it does not look like the cards.
options.kept: Fixed slots: controls never move, only their state changes.

options.label: Ebru Bath
options.thesis: The maze floats on a pigment bath you comb through.
options.viewport: Card floating on a marbled bath that ripples on each move.
options.case: Fuses poorly: soft liquid marks clash with the cards' hard ink outlines, and nobody in this audience knows it.
options.kept: One surface: navigation is staying on the table, not changing pages.

options.label: Polish Film Poster
options.thesis: One painted metaphor swallows the screen.
options.viewport: A painted metaphor frames the card.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a painted metaphor would compete with the card, which must stay the protagonist.
options.risk: Steals the stage from the card.
options.kept: The hottest colour is reserved for the one thing in focus.

options.label: Lexicon Plate
options.thesis: Text columns with colour quarantined in bordered plates.
options.viewport: Cards as plates beside a column of entries.
options.case: Fuses poorly: built on reading, which this game avoids.
options.kept: Colour quarantined: only the card carries colour; the UI is ink.

options.label: Memory Quilt
options.thesis: Every card a patch, stitched into one quilt.
options.viewport: Picker as a quilt of card patches.
options.case: Fuses poorly: soft cloth texture clashes with ink-and-flat-colour cards.
options.kept: Provenance stays visible: each card carries its artist credit.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.thesis: Levels as glazed cups on a shelf.
options.viewport: Cards in a shelf row; spots drip glaze.
options.case: Fuses poorly: unrelated to the cards and hard for kids to read.
options.kept: States as visible physical stages, not labels.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A casual mobile puzzle game, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: Level grid with numbered bubbles and stars; play with a big chunky pause button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every puzzle app and nothing like the cards.
